where: AD-6 — the "Record law" paragraph against the telemetry exemption in "The closed store list" (ARCHITECTURE-SPINE.md lines 124 and 122)
side_a: **Record law.** Every durable record carries `occurred_at` and `recorded_at`, both int64 UTC nanoseconds from `qmf-core`'s clock, plus its announcement `journal_seq`;
side_b: The telemetry store is the one declared store the announcement law exempts: a telemetry append emits no journal event, because observability is not the ledger (P-12, AD-23) and a journal that is never trimmed (AD-8) may not grow with a stream that is bounded.
divergence: A telemetry record is a durable record in one of AD-6's own declared independent stores, so the record law demands it carry an announcement `journal_seq` — while the announcement exemption means no announcement, and therefore no `journal_seq`, ever exists for it. Builder A obeys the record law: every trace, metric and trajectory record schema carries `journal_seq`, and the daemon must allocate that sequence — i.e. emit an announcement — per telemetry append, so the never-trimmed evidence journal grows one entry per span, exactly the growth AD-6, AD-8 and AD-23 forbid. Builder B obeys the exemption: the telemetry record schema has no `journal_seq` at all and the journal stays free of telemetry. The two products ship different telemetry record shapes and different journals; AD-6's cross-store fold law ("the announcement's `journal_seq` is the ordering key in every fold that spans stores") resolves on A and is unresolvable on B, and a telemetry store written by one cannot be read or ordered by the other's code.
fix: Replace the opening clause of AD-6's Record law with: "**Record law.** Every durable record carries `occurred_at` and `recorded_at`, both int64 UTC nanoseconds from `qmf-core`'s clock, plus — in every store the announcement law binds — its announcement `journal_seq`; a telemetry record, whose store that law exempts, carries `occurred_at` and `recorded_at`, no `journal_seq`, and is ordered by `recorded_at` and its `correlation_id` alone (AD-23);" (rest of the sentence unchanged: "every externally-sourced fact additionally carries `source` and `revision`, so a knowledge-time bound is declarable everywhere.")

where: AD-11 constraint sentence against AD-10's `HookResult` field list (ARCHITECTURE-SPINE.md lines 204 and 190)
side_a: its `HookResult` may carry `decision` and `reason` and nothing else, and the validator rejects at registration any agent-authored hook whose result type can carry `updated_input`, `updated_output`, `injected_context` or `ledger_entry`.
side_b: `ledger_entry` (`before_task_complete` and `review_required` only, and that entry still passes `before_ledger_append` like every other append) and `verifier_ref` (`before_task_complete` and `review_required` only).
divergence: `HookResult` has seven fields (`decision`, `reason`, `updated_input`, `updated_output`, `injected_context`, `ledger_entry`, `verifier_ref`); AD-11's registration validator enumerates only four of the five it must reject, omitting `verifier_ref`. Builder A implements the rule ("nothing else") and rejects an agent-authored hook whose result type can carry any of the five. Builder B implements the enumerated mechanism as written — AD-11 declares its constraints "mechanical, not aspirational" — and registers an agent-authored, mission-scoped hook on `before_task_complete` or `review_required` whose result carries `verifier_ref`, letting the Mission's own agent name the deterministic verifier script for its own completion gate (AD-10: "completion runs a deterministic verifier script rather than an LLM judging itself"). Identical hook templates get opposite registration outcomes, and the two builds disagree on who chooses a Task's completion verifier — the privilege escalation AD-11's Prevents line exists to close.
fix: Replace the AD-11 clause with: "its `HookResult` may carry `decision` and `reason` and nothing else, and the validator rejects at registration any agent-authored hook whose result type can carry `updated_input`, `updated_output`, `injected_context`, `ledger_entry` or `verifier_ref` — the five non-`decision`/`reason` fields of AD-10's tagged union, enumerated here so the check is closed."

where: AD-22 "Role splits" clause against AD-6's definition-store enumeration and AD-8's Definition store row (ARCHITECTURE-SPINE.md lines 276, 122 and 151)
side_a: Role splits: `role.base` is operator-authored and immutable to the pipeline, versioned only by a human commit; `role.overlay` is proposal-editable (appended prompt sections, added skills, narrowed toolsets).
side_b: AD-6 closed store list: "Desk, Role (`role.base` and `role.overlay`) and Quant records (AD-7)" … "each a projection over its own `noun.verb` journal events with `journal_seq` as its ordering key" — and AD-8's Definition store row, who-may-write cell: "daemon only, as journal projections; agents propose edits only as AD-22 RefinementProposals".
divergence: AD-6 and AD-8 place `role.base` inside the definition store as a journal-event projection whose only writer is the daemon; AD-22 says the same record is "versioned only by a human commit", a VCS write path with no journal event, no store row and no wire command. Builder A ships role.base as repo-tracked role files loaded at daemon start — no `role.*` journal events, no `journal_seq` ordering, nothing for AD-6's fold or AD-27's restore to rebuild, and a definition store whose Role member exists outside the closed store list AD-6 closes with "A store not on this list may not be created". Builder B ships a wire command that writes a `role.updated` journal event — and, because AD-24's human-gate list is declared "the sole authority on which commands require that principal" and names no Role write (it names `desk.create`/`quant.create`, `desk.moved`, a Quant record write, a Routine record write and an `ExecutionEnvironment` declaration write), that command is accepted from a `machine` principal, so a plugin or scheduler can rewrite `role.base`, the capability ceiling AD-16 narrows every Agent from. Different owner, different write path, different data shape and opposite enforcement on the one record that bounds every Agent's tools.
fix: Replace the AD-22 clause with: "Role splits: `role.base` is operator-authored and immutable to the pipeline — it is a definition-store record like every other (AD-6), written only by an `operator`-principal `role.set_base` wire command recording a `role.updated` journal event, never by an agent, a plugin, a hook or any other `machine` principal, and never by this pipeline, whatever a human commits upstream of that command; `role.overlay` is proposal-editable (appended prompt sections, added skills, narrowed toolsets)." And in AD-24's closed human-gate list, insert after "`desk.create` and `quant.create` (AD-7),": "a `role.base` write (AD-16, AD-22),".
